fragments.text: It is indeed my honour and privilege to be speaking at the UNESCO event on information for all program with a focus on information accessibility. And today we will be hearing lot of experts with regard to how AI is helping bridge the gap of accessibility and ensuring information accessible for all. In the session today I will be speaking mainly about how artificial intelligence is transforming forming this aspect of digital economy and digital accessibility and use of AI for making information better accessible for various services. I would also be highlighting about what India has been doing in the field of AI and how India is poised to take advantage of the AI revolution happening world over. Artificial intelligence has become a part and parcel of all our lives.

Every day whenever we browse the internet or any service knowingly and knowingly we using an AI based service. Like for example, when people are watching a YouTube video it will give recommendations for other videos to watch, people are watching Netflix, they will get recommendations all of it based on AI. There are a lot of language related translations which is happening in the field of AI and like for example, when you use your Alexa and the series and all it's all an AI that's answering the queries and CRN solutions, the AI chatbots have become very popular on all our portals including government portals where in like when you are going to the railways website

if you want to ask a query there is a chatbot that comes at the AI Disha bot that there on the railways website for COVID-19 my gov was also using AI in a big way in the sense that the COVID-19 the my gov corona help desk which was built with AI based chatbot which allowed people to get information about COVID information about vaccination it allowed people to download vaccination certificates it allowed people to book vaccination slots so there is a lot of AI that is happening all around. So, AI is not something that is the technology of the future, it is happening right now, right here, not only across the world, but within India also and more and more people are using it. When the potential of AI is counted,

the contribution that it can make to the digital economy has been estimated to be almost 950 million dollars for Indian economy by 2030. But the global economy estimates range from $15 billion to $20 billion of contributions to come from AI. So, given the strength that India has in regard to AI related workforce, India is actually adequately poised to take advantage of this growth in AI that is happening across the world. We are amongst one of the largest providers of AI workforce. Globally, we are amongst one of the largest AI based startup nation which helps in building AI based solutions for the world. In the field of health, we have seen how Indian startups have built solutions that helps use of AI for diagnosing diseases

like diabetic naturopathy, breast cancer. It has been used for cataract detections in Tamil Nadu. In agriculture, AI has been used for crop predictions using data that comes from various sources and using it for making better crop productions for the farmers. AI has also been used in the natural language translation machine in which it is used for natural language processing and helping Indians communicate with Indians in their own native language. The potential of AI in the days to come in enabling the next 500 billion Indians to get on board to AI to internet is going to be immense because right now the majority of the people have this bottleneck of not knowing English language in which most of the portals

are there or not knowing how to browse the AI seeks to address these two issues by enabling voice-based internet by allowing people to talk to a platform and talk and get services on it. On the Umang platform that we have been implementing in National Legal Division, Mr. Ronitson IT, we're building AI-based chatbot and a voice what we're in. You could talk to the Umang app and get information and get services in regards to various public services the government offers. So for example you'll be able to talk to the Umang app and say that what are the status of my passport number, when will I get my PAN card, how will I get a driving license and you will get voice based responses and you will be able to access those services

with that mode. So, AI is the central to our strategy and based on that India launched its national strategy on AI because in the 18th it focused on the AI for all approach and the mantra for that was that how do we ensure AI brings in more equitable access to services for all citizens. The other key focus in the AI national strategy on AI was to was to ensure that India emerges as a garage for the world for AI based solutions. With any solution that is built and developed and deployed in India will for all purposes we will be reusable in any other part of the world and part of this trend comes from the huge data that we have for any public service

given our population, given our scale, the amount of data that's available with us, the amount of data analytics that can be built on that and based on machine learning or the algorithms AI based solutions are built. And the India's AI based solution being used in the field of smart mobility if you look at the kind of solution that has been deployed in smart city that also the companies which have deployed it are building the solutions for other countries also. And as I mentioned healthcare also it is happening in the same way. One area that we need to address in order to ensure that India gets the AI leadership in the world is to promote AI based research, to promote availability of supercomputers,

to allow researchers and entrepreneurs to run their algorithms and to push forward for ensuring adequate capacity at all levels for building AI solutions. For this objective we are implementing the schemes like the vicious area PhD scheme in which PhD scholars are being trained to in AI based solutions and they are helping us get patents and get deploy AI based solutions that can be used in various applications. CDAC is building the super computers required for AI based computing that we call it AIRAVAC which is going to be commissioned soon and that would allow a facility that can be used by all our entrepreneurs and researchers for running their algorithms. Similarly for building capacity in the field of AI, especially in the government,

we have run several programs like the AI paid church or we organize the responsible AI for social empowerment summit last year which saw participation of more than 80,000 people from almost 81 countries across the world and that showed what India's strength is in building AI based solutions at scale. For upscaling government, with the government team members in the field of AI, we have launched the Digital India Dialogue series in which we get partners from academia and partners from industry to give, to showcase and demos of AI based solutions that can be customized and adopted across the country. In order to look at the future and to ensure that we are able to build an AI based workforce,

the responsible AI for youth program was launched in which we are partnering with industry to train school students in building AI based solutions. And after the success of program last year, this year we extended it to only government school kids in the 4th class of 9th to 12th and we were surprised to get more than 50,000 students sign up for this program out of which 11,000 students have already completed the program and the top 100 are building their AI based solutions that will be showcased very soon. Then CVSC has been in touch with industry and they have included AI as the curriculum in class 10 and 12 and students are getting their AI lessons right from the beginning and recently CVSC also

launched a program to train 1 million children in the field of AI in order to ensure that these children when they go to college and when they go to when they join the workforce they are already have the skill sets required for building AI based solutions. So overall AI has been the focus in the government, a national program on AI has been conceptualized which will have a wrong way De Ravath and wrong way cap city building in other programs which include building up in the Indian Center for Transformation, AI in Partition with Industry free and it would also have some moonshot projects which will take up projects in the field of agriculture, healthcare, smart cities, natural language processing that will showcase

what all India and Indians can build for pushing forward the cause of AI. So AI in the days to come will be a mainstay of our entire approach and I am sure that with the amount of investment the government and the private sector is making in the field of AI will have many more unicorns coming in AI based solutions and public services be transformed with the use of AI making them more accessible making them more affordable making them more intuitive and people will benefit greatly from the AI based solutions.
